problem: Given that  $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ -5 & -7\end{aligned}]$ has the LU decomposition $A=LU,$ then $L=$
worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $A$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $A$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ -5 & -7\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+5{R}_{1}\,⟺\,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot D \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 0 & 18\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{1}A=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}A & =U \\ A & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ A & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 5 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ A & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -5 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 0 & 18\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$
